svg.text: One program, 51 languages — does GitGalaxy count it the same everywhere?
The same 12-probe program, written in every language. The engine should extract the same counts from each;
every dot is one language's deviation from the cross-language median. Red is an open engine defect — a rule matching the wrong construct,
or a scoring weight sitting inside a count — the work left. Grey is a documented variation: the language cannot express the construct,

a deliberate scoring choice, or an echo of another row. Each row's bar: in band (±25% of the median) · documented · open defect; the badge prints the accounted share — everything that is not an open defect.
average share in band, 54 gated metrics
cells with no verdict at all
n/a — no rule for this language
strip: median at the centre · shaded band ±25% · ticks ±50% · clipped at ±110% · open-defect languages named above the strip, documented ones below (not-gated rows: beyond ±50%)
the slicer: functions, parameters, classes and dependency edges — the spread of one program's counts across languages, not recall
one rule per signal; every count here was planted on purpose, in every language
rules the risk formulas read that the corpus never plants — nothing here was written, so every language should read 0
graph measures over the same three planted imports (pagerank_score = pagerank; shown once)
per-function and census measures derived from the signals

what the product reports, per file — the gitgalaxy#2991 vector vocabulary (connectivity, mutation_surface, ...) over the frozen risk_* columns; banded within the strictness stratum where a constant is read
how long the same program came out, and how the language spells it: token and keyword tallies, and the ratios that divide by them
gitgalaxy#2994 fam_* raw sums — each signal grouped into its surface family; context, since the families fold in signals the SPEC never plants
unit totals the per-unit risk ratios read (gitgalaxy#2908); gated per file by the manifests, reported here as attribution edges
* not gated: languages vary too much in how they express this — program length, token vocabulary, inputs the corpus does not plant, commit age — for a cross-language band to mean anything.
Shown for context, never scored. Every dot outside the band on a gated row has a verdict in deviation_ledger.json; the cause behind each colour is in docs/bias_data.json (cell_categories).

Inert — recorded but drawn nowhere: fam_crypto, fam_regex, fam_time, llm_api, risk_spec_match, risk_stability, state_slop_duplicates — every language reads exactly 0 (the corpus plants nothing for them), so the column asks no cross-language question.
keyword-rosetta · tools/bias_report.py · band ±25% of the cross-language median (exact agreement where the median is 0) · cause categories: gitgalaxy docs/contract_roadmap.md
